WATCH: 𝗛𝗜𝗠𝗔𝗥𝗦 𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲‑𝗳𝗶𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝗻 𝗡𝘂𝗲𝘃𝗮 𝗘𝗰𝗶𝗷𝗮

For the first time, the U.S. Army’s 25th Infantry Division rapidly forward‑deployed a full High Mobility Artillery Rocket System (HIMARS) in the Philippines. Brig. Gen. Jonathan Velishka called it remarkable: “The division only fielded this capability last July. From then to today, our artillery integrated new equipment, trained Soldiers, and forward‑deployed here for qualification and certification.”

The 2nd Battalion, 11th Long Range Fires Battalion moved to Laur, Nueva Ecija on April 15‑16, firing 12 precision rockets before an audience of Philippine Army officers, civilians, and media. Philippine Army support was crucial—securing firing points and impact areas to ensure safety.

Maj. Gen. Michael Logico of the AFP Training and Doctrine Command likened the experience to Olympic training: “You’re not gonna be a world‑class swimmer unless you train with a world‑class partner.”

This first‑ever HIMARS live‑fire in Laur introduced new doctrine, firing lanes, and impact areas for the Philippine Army, underscoring growing U.S.–PH interoperability and a shared commitment to defense readiness.

📹📷 U.S. Army 25th Infantry Division
